method: Read-only official SEC source and current first-party competitor/pricing review.
hypothesis: A point-in-time filing diff/event API has a narrow uncommoditized output worth a 100-issuer local prototype.

observed.raw_source: SEC submissions and XBRL JSON are public, unauthenticated, rapidly updated, accession-addressable and available as nightly bulk archives under declared-user-agent and rate policies.
observed.marketplace_signal: The durable snapshot found 25 SEC results, 40 aggregate monthly users, a free leader with 15 users and no paid result with five users.
exact_substitutes: Apify canonical-section change detector with previous-period/amendment pairing, deterministic hunks, stable IDs, bounded evidence and source links
FilingDiff visual section diffs, evidence quotes, PDFs and alerts
sec-api.io streaming, section extraction, XBRL conversion and structured 8-K events
SEC Daily API commercial filing infrastructure

optimistic_economics.warning: The exact competitor has one monthly user and no ratings; paying status, revenue and margin are unknown.

reason: The output is already commoditized, buyer demand is absent, and the proposed 100-issuer build would measure parser feasibility rather than economic demand.
reopening_conditions: Multiple independent buyers identify the same unmet workflow.
A source/schema change creates a genuinely new provenance capability.
A 12-pair adversarial fixture demonstrates an output absent from the named substitutes and buyer evidence supports sufficient volume.
smallest_reopened_experiment: Twelve immutable filing pairs: four ordinary prior-year pairs, four original/amendment pairs and four adversarial structural pairs, with manually reviewed section/hunk oracles and deterministic stable-ID gates.
